The 2026 ORSC is mandatory from April 1, 2027. The deck guide the county posts is the Oregon Prescriptive Deck Guide 2023 (2023 ORSC).

Decks whose walking surface is not more than 30 in. above adjacent grade at any point within 3 ft horizontally are exempt from permit (ORSC R105.2, per the deck guide).
The applicant must attach a site-specific Oregon Design Criteria Hub summary report to the deck guide.

From that report, check the deck guide boxes: ground snow ≤ 40, 50, 60 or 70 psf; frost line depth 12, 18 or 24 in.; weathering moderate (3,000 psi concrete) or severe (3,500 psi); decay slight or moderate.
The lateral load connection is either four 750 lb hold-down tension devices or two 1,500 lb devices (R507.9.2).
Guards are 36 in. minimum, with openings that block a 4 in. sphere.

A site/plot plan is required for every building permit. It must be at a measurable scale on 11×17 in. paper with a north arrow, and show setbacks, corner elevations (2 ft contours), easements and the full footprint including decks and exterior stairs.
Plan sheets must be no larger than 2×3 ft and no smaller than 11×17 in. Upload each sheet as a single landscape PDF page, numbered 001, 002 and so on, with a page title.
Floor plans must show balconies and decks 30 in. above grade (Residential Building Permit Checklist).

The frost depth of 12 in. comes from the county's 'Engineering Structural Design Criteria' sheet, which is dated 01/01/2015 and written for the 2014 OSSC: 12 in. minimum below 500 ft elevation, and 18 in. at or above 500 ft unless the building official requires deeper. That sheet is still linked from the Residential Buildings page. It also lists Vult 120 mph (Risk Category II, ASCE 7-10) and 1,500 psf default bearing for engineered work. In a Fire Hazard Severity Zone or WUI area, the County's 2026 Fire Hazard Notes (2025 CWUIC Ch. 5) say deck, porch, balcony and stair walking surfaces must be one of: ignition-resistant material or material meeting SFM 12-7A-4 plus Sec. 503.2.4; fire-retardant-treated wood labeled for exterior use per CBC 2303.2; noncombustible material; material meeting SFM 12-7A-4A where the attached exterior wall covering is noncombustible or ignition-resistant; or material meeting ASTM E2632 and ASTM E2726 (Sec. 504.7.3.2).

Title 30 amends CWUIC 501.1 so that additions, alterations and repairs to existing buildings in any FHSZ or WUI area must meet the WUI rules when the permit application is filed on or after January 1, 2026. It also removes the exception for buildings built before July 1, 2008.

Attached or detached accessory structures within 50 ft of an applicable building (trellises, arbors, patio covers, gazebos and similar) must be noncombustible, ignition-resistant or heavy timber (CWUIC 504.11, per the County fire notes).
Title 26 Sec. 106.3 says that permit-exempt work is still regulated by the WUI (Chapter 7A) rules. The County ordinance does not change the deck-exemption wording itself.
Title 26 Sec. 108.4.9 requires an inspection of the impervious moisture barrier on weather-exposed balconies and elevated walking surfaces before it is concealed.
The County's hillside-building seismic provisions (Title 26 Sec. 1613.9) exempt decks that do not support, and are not supported by, the main building.

The County's residential minimum plan list (2/1/2026) asks for drawings to scale (1/8 in. min., 1/4 in. recommended) on 18x24 in. min. sheets (24x36 recommended). It also asks for a dimensioned site plan with all structure-to-property-line setbacks, dimensioned structural, framing and foundation plans, and sections. That list is written for new SFR/MFR work, not decks specifically.

The City of Los Angeles (LADBS) was not checked because web search was exhausted and its bulletin listings load only through JavaScript. For a real address, get the seismic category and wind speed site-specifically (ASCE 7 hazard tool) or ask LA County Building & Safety.

deck_notes: Decks, walks and driveways not more than 30 in. above adjacent grade, not over a basement or story below, and not part of an accessible route need no building permit (County Building Code exemption list, item 9). No area limit is stated.

PDS 044 'Residential Decks' (rev. 01/01/2023) is a standard plan for single-family decks only. It must come with a plot plan per PDS 090 and be used together with PDS 081 (Minimum Construction Specifications) and PDS 075 (Guards and Handrails).

PDS 044 design limits: 60 psf live load; no hot tubs or other heavy concentrated loads; 10 ft max post height; no support from an overhang or cantilever; no window, door or opening wider than 4 ft under a deck supported by the existing building.

PDS 044 typical post footing on undisturbed firm soil: 12 in. below grade and 6 in. above grade; 18x18 in. for posts at 8 ft o.c. or 20x20 in. at 10 ft o.c.; concrete f'c 2,500 psi min.; deck stair footing 12 in. min. deep and 12 in. wide.
PDS 044 sets a 7 ft minimum horizontal distance from the bottom leading edge of a footing to daylight (slope face).
PDS 044 ledger at rim joist: min. 3x ledger with 5/16 or 3/8 in. lag bolts at 8 in. o.c., flashing above and below, joists in hangers.

PDS 044 framing: 4x8 min. joists with a 12 ft max span, at 32 in. o.c. with 2x fire-retardant-treated decking or 16 in. o.c. (or per the product listing) with alternative decking; 4x10 or 6x8 min. beams; 6x6 posts; knee braces required on decks 4 ft and higher.

PDS 044 materials: Douglas Fir-Larch No. 2 or better; preservative-treated joists within 18 in. of grade and girders within 12 in.; fasteners in treated wood must be hot-dip galvanized, stainless steel, silicon bronze or copper.

The County's guard handout (PDS 075) requires guards where a walking surface is more than 30 in. above grade, at least 42 in. high, with openings that stop a 4 in. sphere. Stair handrails are 34-38 in. above nosings, and the PDS 044 stair section shows a 42 in. guard.

PDS 044 stairs: 36 in. min. width, 6 ft 8 in. min. headroom, 36 in. min. landings top and bottom, risers 4 to 7-3/4 in., 10 in. min. treads, 3/4 to 1-1/4 in. nosings where treads are under 11 in., 4x12 stringers at 48 in. max. spacing.

PDS 044 says it meets WUI fire-resistive requirements, with decking of 2x approved fire-retardant-treated lumber or an alternative material meeting the County code. It cites County Building Code 92.1.709A.1.4, a pre-2026 section number.

The 2026 County WUI Code Sec. 504.7.3.2 says deck, porch, balcony and stair walking surfaces must be one of: material meeting ASTM E2632/E2726 per 504.7.3.3; material meeting SFM 12-7A-4 plus Sec. 503.2.4; noncombustible material; material meeting SFM 12-7A-4A with a noncombustible or ignition-resistant attached wall (with a Class B flame-spread exception); or material meeting 504.7.3.4 per ASTM E2632 with the same wall condition.
The County WUI Code applies to all unincorporated SRA land in Moderate, High and Very High FHSZs, plus locally designated VHFHSZ and WUI areas.

Plot plan (PDS 090, rev. 07/24/2026): two sets on 18x24 in. min. sheets (11x17 for minor permits and small additions), drawn to an engineer's scale, with north arrow, vicinity map, all property-line dimensions, required setbacks, easements, drainage and stormwater BMPs.
No coastal or Coastal Commission requirements appear in the County deck handouts.
counties.note: The frost depth is the County table's 'Minimum 12-inch footing depth' (no frost-line figure is given). counties.edition: 2024 IRC with AMC Chapter 23.85 local amendments (AO 2026-33, as amended, passed Apr 14, 2026, effective 30 days after passage, about May 14, 2026); the 2018 IRC preceded it
counties.wind_basis: Per site from the Anchorage Bowl 'Three Second Gust' Wind Zone Map (AMC 23.85 Figure R301.2(2)), which replaces the IRC map. Legend (minimum ultimate speeds, Risk Category I / II / III-IV): Zone I 120/130/135, Zone II 135/145/150, Zone III 145/155/160, Zone IV 150/160/165 mph. deck_notes: A permit is required for any deck over 30 in. above finished grade, whether attached to or detached from the residence (Handout R.13).
Decks may be built to the American Wood Council Prescriptive Residential Wood Deck Construction Guide.

The plot plan must be an as-built drawing sealed by an Alaska-registered land surveyor, to scale, showing the house, the deck and stairs and their distances from all lot lines, easements, utilities and overhead wires.
Footing depth follows AMC 23.85 Table R403.1: cold (unheated) exterior isolated foundations and piers need 120 in., or 60 in. in non-frost-susceptible material; warm perimeter footings need 42 in.

Attached decks, landings and platforms no more than 72 in. above grade may bear directly on the ground unless an exterior door swings outward onto them; frost heave must be considered (Table R403.1 note 3).
Frost protection is not required for deck stair footings that are not attached to or in contact with the frost-protected structure (AMC 23.85.R507.3.3).
Deck framing exposed to weather must be pressure-preservative-treated or naturally durable, with hot-dip galvanized or stainless fasteners.

Deck beams and joists not protected like a roof need decay protection unless fully painted or stained and capped with 24-gauge galvanized flashing over ice-and-water shield (AMC 23.85.R304.1 item 10).

Plans must show the ledger-to-house connection (fastener diameter, length and spacing), ledger flashing, joist uplift clips, post and beam connector part numbers, bracing, and a lateral tie-back to the house.
The IRC ledger flashing rule (R507.9.1.5) is amended locally to 1 in. down the exterior ledger face instead of 4 in.

Guards are required where the walking surface is more than 30 in. above grade within 36 in. horizontally. They must be at least 36 in. high with openings smaller than a 4 in. sphere, resist 200 lb on the top rail, and resist 50 lb on infill (Handout R.13; IRC R507.10 is deleted locally).
Deck snow load is determined per section R301.2.3 instead of Table R301.2 (AMC 23.85.R507.1).
counties.note: frost_depth_in = 120 is the code minimum for a cold exterior isolated foundation (deck piers/footings) in AMC 23.85 Table R403.1. It may be 60 in. in non-frost-susceptible material (note 5). The 'frost line' in Table R301.2 just points to this table; 42 in. is the warm perimeter value. Ground snow load is 50 psf allowable / 80 psf ultimate (for ASCE 7). Handout R.13 is dated May 7, 2021 (written under the 2018 code) but is still the posted deck handout. Permits are issued by Anchorage Building Safety within its building safety service area.

counties.jurisdiction: City and County of Honolulu Department of Planning and Permitting (DPP); ROH Chapter 16 (building code) and Chapter 18 (permits)
counties.edition: 2018 IRC as the Hawaii State Residential Code with State and City amendments (Ordinance 24-15), effective 08/09/2024, plus City Addendum #1 effective 03/11/2025 (per the DPP 'Codes Currently in Effect' table)
counties.wind_basis: Honolulu Table R301.2(1): wind speed 'Per Figure R301.2(8) State Residential Code'. IRC wind provisions may be used only where the effective ultimate design wind speed Veff_ult is below 140 mph; at 140 mph or more the alternative provisions/wind design apply and windborne debris protection is required (Honolulu Table R301.2.1).
deck_notes: Open slat wood decks must have at least 6 in. of ground clearance for any wood member (ROH amendment R317.6 exception).
Wood protected from decay must be preservative-treated per AWPA U1 (amended R317.1).
Fasteners in non-borate pressure-treated or fire-retardant-treated wood must be hot-dip zinc-coated galvanized steel, stainless steel, silicon bronze or copper (amended R317.3.1).

Termite protection follows the Formosan-termite rules: soil treatment at the maximum label rate by a licensed operator, or approved barriers such as basaltic termite barrier or stainless mesh, where wood framing sits on slabs or foundations (R318.1.3, R318.2, R318.3 amendments).

Plan sheets must be at least 36 x 24 in., all the same size, landscape, black and white, drawn to scale with a graphic scale bar, and must leave a blank 5.75 x 3.75 in. DPP stamp space at the top right of each sheet.
The plot plan must show the entire parcel with TMK lot dimensions, building and yard setbacks, easements, and the location and scope of the work.
Decks are not on DPP's list of commonly applicable permit exemptions (see ROH 18-3.1(b) for the full list).
Stamped plans are required when, for example, work on a one-story residence exceeds $180,000 or the site is in a special management or flood hazard area.
counties.note: Honolulu's amended Table R301.2(1) has no ground snow load or frost line depth columns: it lists only wind, seismic, weathering, termite, decay (Moderate to severe) and flood hazards (FEMA). So frost_depth_in and ground_snow_psf are null, with no published local value. The IRC footing-depth rule R403.1.4 is not amended by Honolulu; a Hawaii County DPW procedure quotes it as 12 in. below undisturbed ground (2006 text), but no Honolulu source stating a number was opened. The State table R301.2(4) assigns Oahu SDC D0, while Honolulu's table says 'C or D0'. The ROH sections on American Legal returned 403, so the ordinance PDF (Ord. 24-15, from hnldoc) was used.

counties.jurisdiction: County of Hawaii Department of Public Works, Building Division; Hawaii County Code Chapter 5 (administrative), 5A (building) and 5B (residential)
counties.edition: 2018 IRC per Hawaii County Code Chapter 5B 'Residential Building Code' (Ord. 21-61, 2021; code supplement 11, 1-2022). Chapter 5A (non-residential and post/pier raised floors) is still the 2006 IBC (Ord. 20-61, amended by 21-61).
counties.wind_basis: Hawaii County Table R301.2(1): wind speed 'Per Figure R301.2(8)' (county ultimate wind speed maps). IRC wind provisions may be used only where Vult is below 130 mph, or below 140 mph for single-story slab-on-grade buildings in Exposure B (HCC 5B amended R301.2.1).
deck_notes: Detached decks or platforms less than 30 in. above grade are exempt from a building permit, but must still meet the zoning 'yards' setbacks (HCC 5-3-22(a)(1)(C)).
Raised floor systems on post or pier foundations must be designed under the Chapter 5A building code, not the IRC prescriptive rules (HCC 5B amended R401.5).
Open slat wood decks must have at least 6 in. of ground clearance for any wood member (HCC 5B R408.8).
Decay protection must use naturally durable wood approved by the building official or wood preservative-treated per AWPA U1 (amended R317.1).
Termite protection needs one of chemical termiticide, a baiting system or a physical barrier, plus one of treated wood, cold-formed steel or naturally durable termite-resistant wood (amended R318.1).

Footings must be at least 12 in. below undisturbed ground except on solid rock (DPW Division Procedure 2017-0602, citing R403.1.4); embedment in in-situ basalt is waived only for slab-on-grade footings.
Plans should be 22x34, 24x36 or 34x44 in. sheets, all the same size, landscape, to scale, with a 6 x 6 in. DPW block on the cover, submitted digitally through EPIC.
The site plan must show distances to property lines and other buildings, access roads and easements, the driveway and utilities.
The design-criteria block on the plans lists basic and effective wind speed, wind exposure category and seismic design category.
counties.note: Seismic design category is D2 in the North and South Kohala, Hamakua and North Hilo districts and E in all other districts (HCC 5B Table R301.2(4)). The county table has no ground snow load or frost depth column, so ground_snow_psf is null; Mauna Kea/Mauna Loa summits were not addressed. frost_depth_in = 12 is the minimum footing depth below undisturbed ground stated in the county's 2017 procedure, which quotes the 2006 IBC/IRC text; HCC 5B does not amend R403.1.4. The county table also lists decay Moderate to severe and flood hazards per FEMA or HCC Chapter 27. A county non-residential checklist still says 'Code Date: IBC 2006 (State projects IBC 2018)'. The 5B text came from the county's Laserfiche records copy of the Hawaii County Code (supp. 11, 1-2022); later amendments are not ruled out. The DPW website itself (dpw.hawaiicounty.gov) returned 403.

counties.jurisdiction: County of Maui Department of Public Works, Development Services Administration (DSA); Maui County Code Chapters 16.25 and 16.26C
counties.edition: 2018 IBC (MCC Chapter 16.26C, Bill 15 CD1 FD1 (2023)) with administrative provisions in MCC Chapter 16.25 (Bill 14 CD1 FD1 (2023)). One- and two-family dwellings 'shall comply with this code or the International Residential Code' (16.25, 101.2.2 exception 1). The IRC edition and county amendments for Maui were not confirmed; the State SBCC notice says the 2018 Hawaii State Residential Code becomes an interim county code where a county has not amended it (HRS 107-28(b)).
counties.wind_basis: State Residential Code: ultimate wind speed per Figure R301.2(5)(b) 'County of Maui, Island of Maui' (also (c) Molokai and (d) Lanai). IRC wind provisions apply only where Vult is below 130 mph.
deck_notes: Detached unroofed decks 30 in. or less from adjacent grade to the deck floor are exempt from a building permit (MCC 16.25, 105.2 item 5, per Bill 14 CD1 FD1 (2023)).

The site plan must show the Tax Map Key number and address, the new construction and existing structures to scale, distances from lot lines, street and finished grades, and flood hazard information. It must be drawn from an accurate boundary survey (16.25, 107.2.6).
Open decks are valued at $40/sq ft and covered decks at $60/sq ft for permit fees (16.25 Table 109.1).
counties.note: The SDC of D1 is the State Residential Code Table R301.2(4) value for the island of Maui; the same table gives Oahu, Molokai and Lanai D0, so Molokai and Lanai in Maui County are D0, not D1. No Maui-specific Table R301.2(1) was found, so weathering, termite, frost and snow are null. mauicounty.gov, Municode and mauicounty.us all returned 403 or a JS challenge. Maui sources are the Bill 14 and Bill 15 (2023) texts from the council's Legistar. The Legistar API shows no passed date for them, but later bills (2024-2026) amend Chapter 16.25, which shows that chapter is in force. Confirm the residential code edition and any Maui design criteria with DSA.
